questions.question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Turn your head quickly to look for other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on your phone.
Changing the radio or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions every mile they drive. Any activity that takes your attention away from driving is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition doesn't cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular checkups.
Know how any medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limitations and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower thinking.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol harm your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: What is a sign that a driver is drunk?

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than normal traffic.
Making sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving too slowly, speeding, jerky motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol's effects may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold remedy could affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts can double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. Wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who drink before driving?

options.text: They are aware of the risks.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they drive more carefully.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, focus, understanding, and reaction time. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, what should you do?

options.text: You cannot exit the freeway.
You can continue through or exit the freeway from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will leave the highway and form an exit ramp. You can change lanes to continue through the interchange, or you must exit the highway if you stay in that lane.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are turning.
Your emergency brake is on.
You are changing lanes.
You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: Stop your car at regular intervals on long trips. Rest and stretch your body, even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful near children. Always give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of both decrease.
The effects of both increase.
It helps cure your illness.
It improves your driving ability.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol or drugs. It is even more dangerous when you combine them.

questions.question: When turning left, who do you yield the right-of-way to?

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers who are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving in bad weather?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help any injured people.
Call the police.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle immediately. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unnecessarily. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency responders.

questions.question: Before turning, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are not important.
They are only found in construction zones.
They provide information to drivers.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. It is the law and a safe driving habit.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The possible speeds for the area.
The maximum or minimum speed allowed by law.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum speed allowed by law.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum safe speed for the road. These limits apply in ideal conditions. You must slow down when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions can reduce your ability to concentrate on driving. If you feel worried, angry, afraid, or upset, wait until you are calm before driving.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, you must pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: How should you safely cross a railroad crossing?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then go if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then go if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Never cross until you are certain it is safe.

questions.question: When can you drive around or under a gate that is lowering or raising at a railroad crossing?

options.text: As long as a train is not too close.
If your vehicle can pass without damaging the gate.
If you look carefully in both directions first.
Never.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, and bells mean you must stop. Do not cross until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a flagger in a construction zone. Failure to do so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if flashing red lights are on, a crossing gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or close enough to be unsafe. If you are unsure whether a train is too close, stop. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If a train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross the tracks. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you encounter an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Speeding up may make them angrier and increase the danger.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A steep grade is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: Traffic signals control traffic and help prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey these signals, unless an officer is directing traffic. When an officer is present, follow the officer's directions instead.
